Render the approved edit in this folder to edit/final.mp4 with the video-use skill. The owner approved the live preview in edit/preview/, so do not change the edit.

Job: client "מאפיית הצפון", job "פרומו לסוף השבוע". The footage folder is the current working directory; treat its files as read-only and write everything to ./edit/.
- Load the skill, then read edit/project.md.
- Render from edit/preview/: npx hyperframes render -q delivery --strict --no-best-effort -o ../final.mp4
- Music: render it as it is. edit/preview/music.mp3 is the music the owner picked (or the silence of No music), and the composition plays it under its volume lane. Never run the music script, and never change, move or re-encode anything in edit/music/ or edit/preview/music.mp3. If the loudness is off, fix it on the render, as the next line says.
- Check the render as the Deliverables row of §0 says: H.264, yuv420p, AAC, −14 LUFS and −1 dBTP, and the composition's duration. Look at a frame at every cut with timeline_view. If the loudness is off, fix it with one static gain and a limiter (field notes), never dynamic loudnorm.
- When captions are burned in, copy their SRT to edit/final.srt.
- Fix only what the render itself broke. If the render shows a problem in the edit, do not re-edit: end with the Blocked: line, naming the problem.

- The job is done when edit/final.mp4 exists and you have checked it. Do not leave anything running in the background when you finish.

This run is unattended (Studio Engine): nobody will answer questions, so never ask any. Follow the skill's §0 and decide on judgment. Notes for this machine:
- Setup is already done: ~/Developer/video-use is cloned with its .venv, and the skill is installed at ~/.claude/skills/video-use. Skip the ln -sfn line in §1 (writes under ~/.claude are blocked here); run the rest of §1's checks.
- This is the local Mac, not a cloud container: work directly in ./edit/ and skip §4 (no staging, device_commit_files or SendUserFile).
- The job path contains spaces and may be Hebrew, so always double-quote paths and variables in Bash (`cd "$SH"`, never `cd $SH`). Never cd or write above ./edit/, and if a cd fails, stop instead of running the next command where you are: a stray folder in the client folder or the inbox gets picked up as a new job.
- Read only this folder. The client's style, this job's series (if it has one) and the shared fonts are already copied into edit/style/, edit/series/ and edit/fonts/, so don't open the client's other folders (other jobs, _Style, _Series, _Fonts) or anything else in the inbox. The one exception is the client's _Shared folder (../_Shared/) when brief.md lists its files: copy the ones you use into edit/shared/ and use them from there.
- macOS tools: Bash is bash 3.2 and sed is BSD sed, so in-place edits need sed -i '' (or use the Edit tool). The edit-video skill is at ~/.claude/skills/edit-video.
- iPhone clips: this ffmpeg has no zscale, so render.py's HLG/HDR tone-map fails; make SDR intermediates first (VideoToolbox scale_vt works here). Keep every clip's orientation: a portrait iPhone clip is stored landscape with a rotation (ffprobe -show_entries stream_side_data=rotation shows e.g. -90). ffmpeg applies that rotation to software-decoded frames only, not to hardware frames (-hwaccel_output_format videotoolbox_vld), so after hwdownload add the turn yourself (transpose=clock for -90, transpose=cclock for 90, hflip,vflip for 180) and check that each intermediate has the width and height the source is shown at.
- The ElevenLabs key is in ~/Developer/video-use/.env, where the transcribe helper reads it. Never print it, copy it or pass it on a command line: everything this run prints is logged.
- If you hit a real blocker, finish what does not depend on it, then make the very last line of your final message start with "Blocked:" followed by one plain sentence naming what is missing, for example "Blocked: ffmpeg is not installed (brew install ffmpeg)." Studio Engine shows that sentence to the user as the job's error.
